language.scope: Initial target: standard SQL/Foundation core query and data semantics from ISO/IEC 9075-2:2023, interpreted through the ISO/IEC 9075-1:2023 framework and the ISO/IEC 9075-11:2023 information/definition schema model where needed. Start with scalar values, NULL and three-valued logic, row/table values, query expressions, predicates, joins, grouping, aggregation, ordering, set operations, schema/catalog state, constraints, and core DDL/DML.
non_goals: Vendor dialect semantics such as PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL, T-SQL, PL/SQL, BigQuery SQL, or DuckDB extensions unless a separate profile is explicitly created.
Physical storage, indexing, query optimization, execution plans, cost models, and performance behavior.
Implementation-specific diagnostics, error wording, collation defaults, limits, or host-environment behavior unless selected as a conformance profile.
Interface and extension parts such as SQL/CLI, SQL/PSM, SQL/MED, SQL/OLB, SQL/JRT, SQL/XML, SQL/MDA, and SQL/PGQ until each is separately scoped.

specifications.title: ISO/IEC 9075-1:2023, Information technology - Database languages SQL - Part 1: Framework (SQL/Framework)
specifications.notes: Defines the conceptual framework, terms, and notation used by the SQL standard series.

specifications.title: ISO/IEC 9075-2:2023, Information technology - Database languages SQL - Part 2: Foundation (SQL/Foundation)
specifications.notes: Primary target for core SQL syntax and semantics. The ISO catalog lists this as a paid 1715-page standard.

specifications.title: ISO/IEC 9075-11:2023, Information technology - Database languages SQL - Part 11: Information and Definition Schemas (SQL/Schemata)
specifications.notes: Relevant for catalog/schema state exposed through standard SQL schemata.

specifications.title: ISO/IEC 9075-9:2023, Part 9: Management of External Data (SQL/MED)
ISO/IEC 9075-13:2023, Part 13: SQL Routines and Types Using the Java Programming Language (SQL/JRT)

reference_implementations.name: No globally accepted SQL reference implementation
reference_implementations.notes: SQL conformance is defined by the ISO/IEC 9075 standard and its feature/profile structure. Vendor systems are dialect implementations and can only serve as selected differential profiles, not as the normative reference.

test_suites.name: Current official public SQL conformance suite
test_suites.notes: Initial research did not identify a current globally accepted public conformance suite for SQL:2023. Historical NIST/FIPS SQL conformance artifacts should be investigated separately before being treated as usable evidence.

test_suites.name: Vendor and research SQL test suites
test_suites.notes: PostgreSQL, SQLite, DuckDB, MySQL, and research suites may be useful for differential and regression testing, but each test must be classified as standard SQL, dialect behavior, implementation-defined behavior, or non-goal.

known_gaps.description: Most ISO/IEC 9075:2023 parts are paid and copyright-protected. The public repo must not vendor or reproduce standard text; implementation work needs licensed access and section-level provenance without copying protected text.
There is no single accepted reference implementation for standard SQL. Differential testing must be profile-based.
No current globally accepted public SQL:2023 conformance test suite has been identified yet.
